_readme: The declared state of the Fab listing. tools/fab_readiness.py measures the built package
against this, so a field left null is reported as an OPEN DECISION rather than silently
passing. Clause numbers refer to the Fab Distribution Agreement of 23 February 2026.
THIS IS JSON, so values need JSON syntax: text in "quotes", true/false rather than YES/NO,
and null for undecided. An invalid file makes fab_readiness fall back to an empty state and
report everything as open, which looks like nothing was ever answered.
_listingPrice: 1(d): your complete discretion, but it must be $0.00 or >= $0.99. No price-parity or
most-favoured-nation clause exists anywhere in the agreement, so nothing here constrains what
createdWithAIReason: A material portion of this plugin was written by a generative model - the C++ handlers, the Blender addon ops, the audit tooling and the documentation were largely authored by Claude working against Andre's direction, review and measurements. 18(k)(ii) asks whether a material portion is generated, not whether it was reviewed afterwards, so the honest answer is yes.
_createdWithAI: 18(k)(ii): REQUIRED where 'a material portion of the Content is generated with Generative AI
Programs'. Not a preference. Answering true here records the decision; you still have to tick
the CreatedWithAI box in the Fab portal itself, which is the thing the clause actually asks for.
_publishedCommit: WHAT IT IS: the git commit hash the live Fab listing was built from - e.g.
WHY IT EXISTS: 3(b) says Fab must get updates no later than any other channel. Recording which
commit is live lets fab_readiness count how many commits HEAD is ahead and tell you whether you
owe Fab an update, instead of you having to remember.
LEAVE IT null UNTIL THE FIRST UPLOAD. Nothing is published yet, so there is no answer. After
you upload, run `git rev-parse HEAD` and paste the result here.
_otherChannels: 3(b): 'If your Content is made available to end users through channels other than the
Marketplaces, you will provide any Updates to Epic no later than you provide them to any other
List every channel that reaches an END USER, as strings. Likely candidates here:
"github-public"      while the repo is public - every push is an update to end users
"github-private"     ONLY if collaborators can pull it; a repo only you pull from is not a
channel, and that is the arrangement that keeps commit-and-push intact
"dds2-sdk-installer" if the SDK bundles the plugin
An empty list means you are declaring that nothing but Fab reaches an end user. Say so only
when it is true - leaving it empty makes 3(b) report UNKNOWN rather than passing.
_licenceInPayload: WHAT IT IS: a decision about the LICENSE file that ships INSIDE the Fab zip. Two valid values:
"fab-eula-notice"  replace it with a short notice pointing at the Fab EULA (recommended)
"mit"              knowingly keep the MIT text in the paid package
WHY IT MATTERS: 3(f)(v) says what ships through Fab is licensed under the Fab EULA and is 'not
superseded by custom licenses included in Content's distributed files'. So the MIT file does
not legally win - the risk is that a BUYER READS IT AND BELIEVES IT. MIT tells them they may
redistribute the plugin publicly, which is the one thing a paid listing depends on them not
SEPARATE QUESTION, NOT THIS FIELD: what licence future PUBLIC versions carry. Every version
pushed so far is MIT to everyone who has ever cloned it, irrevocably - that cannot be undone,
